intervals.label: data taking (partial then full array)
intervals.quote: First physics results are reported from more than 100 surface detector stations.

intervals.label: AugerPrime upgrade
intervals.note: Adds surface scintillator detectors (SSD), upgraded station electronics (UUB), radio antennas (RD) and underground muon counters (UMD) to each existing water-Cherenkov station; RD deployment reported complete November 2024, UMD partial as of the August 2025 status paper. End taken as the month of the AugerPrime status paper (arXiv:2508.08056, submitted 2025-08-11) that describes commissioning of the final components reaching its conclusion; approximate.
intervals.quote: As the commissioning of the final components of AugerPrime reaches its conclusion and the enhanced array comes fully online

name: Pierre Auger Observatory hybrid detector
notes: No per-tank or per-telescope coordinates were recorded in this wave; only the single campus placement point.

placements.note: Placement point is the Observatory campus; the physical array of stations is spread over the surrounding 3000 km² (see site:malargue-auger notes).
placements.quote: Beginning of the construction of the observatory.

description.quote: the 1,660 water surface detector tanks that cover about 3,000 km2 of the Pampa
description.value: Array of 1660 water-Cherenkov detector tanks spread over 3000 km², sampling the particle density of extensive air showers at ground level.

27 optical telescopes in four buildings overlooking the surface array, imaging the ultraviolet fluorescence light emitted by nitrogen molecules excited along an air shower's path through the atmosphere.

summary.plain: A two-in-one detector: 1660 tanks of water spread over 3000 square kilometres sense particles from cosmic-ray showers reaching the ground, while 27 telescopes watch the same showers develop as faint ultraviolet flashes in the night sky.
summary.technical: Hybrid surface-detector/fluorescence-detector system: 1660 water-Cherenkov tanks on a 1.5 km grid across 3000 km², plus 27 fluorescence telescopes in four buildings; currently being upgraded (AugerPrime) with scintillator panels, radio antennas, upgraded electronics and underground muon counters on each surface station.

technology.quote: One technique detects high energy particles through their interaction with water placed in surface detector tanks. The other technique tracks the development of air showers by observing ultraviolet light emitted high in the Earth's atmosphere.
technology.value: Hybrid detector: a surface array of water-Cherenkov tanks sampling air-shower particles at ground level, cross-checked by fluorescence telescopes imaging ultraviolet light from the shower's longitudinal development.
